causal:influence:aco2_activity:negative:.evidence: Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry Ch. 16 (aconitase: citrate -> cis-aconitate -> isocitrate); Boron & Boulpaep Medical Physiology (renal citrate handling) | intervention: do(ACO2 loss-of-function) [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:aco2_activity:negative:.mechanism: Aconitase 2 (ACO2) catalyses the isomerisation of citrate to isocitrate via cis-aconitate in the TCA cycle; reduced ACO2 activity leaves citrate unconsumed, causing it to accumulate — do(ACO2 deficiency) => citrate UP. Citrate is excreted in urine (major urinary organic acid).

causal:influence:aco2_activity:positive:.evidence: Plasma metabolomics in ACO2 deficiency (PMID 28463998, Schwarzmayr et al. 2017 PLOS One): cis-aconitate is a primary diagnostic biomarker reduced in ACO2-deficient patients; infantile cerebellar-retinal degeneration (OMIM 614559) | intervention: do(ACO2 loss-of-function) [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:aco2_activity:positive:.mechanism: ACO2 produces cis-aconitate from citrate; ACO2 deficiency reduces plasma cis-aconitate (PMID 28463998: 36.9-fold decrease). More ACO2 activity => more aconitate produced => higher plasma aconitate.

causal:influence:acth:positive:plasma_dh.evidence: "In vitro ACTH directly stimulates DHEAS and cortisol production, and in vivo excess ACTH is clearly involved in driving the high androgen concentrations seen in fetuses affected with CAH." Williams Textbook of Endocrinology, 14th ed., ch 23, p 839
causal:influence:acth:positive:plasma_dh.mechanism: ACTH binds MC2R on fetal adrenal fetal zone cells -> activates StAR -> increases DHEA sulfation to DHEAS

causal:influence:agat_activity:positive:.evidence: Lehninger, creatine biosynthesis; OMMBID AGAT (GATM) deficiency — DECREASED guanidinoacetate
causal:influence:agat_activity:positive:.mechanism: AGAT (GATM) transfers the amidino group of arginine to glycine forming guanidinoacetate; reduced AGAT activity lowers guanidinoacetate

causal:influence:agps_activity:positive:.evidence: Rhizomelic chondrodysplasia punctata type 3 (RCDP3) OMIM 600121 (AGPS LoF); Wanders & Waterham, Annu Rev Biochem 2006 (plasmalogen deficiency in peroxisomal disorders); Motley et al., Nat Genet 1997 (AGPS mutations cause RCDP3). | intervention: AGPS loss-of-function (RCDP type 3, OMIM 600121): AGPS LoF -> ether lipid / plasmalogen synthesis failure -> severe plasma plasmalogen deficiency
causal:influence:agps_activity:positive:.mechanism: Alkyldihydroxyacetonephosphate synthase (AGPS) catalyzes the first ether-bond-forming step in plasmalogen biosynthesis in peroxisomes. AGPS deficiency (rhizomelic chondrodysplasia punctata type 3, RCDP3) causes severe reduction of plasmalogens in plasma and red blood cells. More AGPS activity supports greater plasmalogen synthesis.

causal:influence:agrp_npy_tone:negative:.evidence: INTERVENTIONAL (genetic). AgRP overexpression / leptin-deficient disinhibition lowers MC4R signalling and drives hyperphagia. DRAFT for domain review.
causal:influence:agrp_npy_tone:negative:.mechanism: AgRP is an MC4R inverse agonist/antagonist (quality: AgRP tone -> disposition: competitive MC4R blockade -> process: reduced MC4R signalling -> quality: MC4R signalling)

causal:influence:agt_activity:negative:u.evidence: Scriver's OMMBID / Saudubray — PH1 (AGXT, OMIM 259900): elevated urinary glycolate + oxalate is the diagnostic signature
causal:influence:agt_activity:negative:u.mechanism: in PH1 the diverted glyoxylate is also reduced to glycolate, raising urinary glycolate; reduced AGT activity raises it

causal:influence:agt_activity:negative:u.evidence: Primary hyperoxaluria type 1 (AGXT; OMIM 259900): glyoxylate accumulation is the proximate metabolic event (Scriver's OMMBID / Saudubray, Inborn Metabolic Diseases — PH1: glyoxylate accumulates and is diverted to oxalate and glycolate); Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry (glyoxylate metabolism) | intervention: do(AGT / AGXT loss-of-function)
causal:influence:agt_activity:negative:u.mechanism: AGT transaminates glyoxylate to glycine (substrate consumption); AGT deficiency leaves glyoxylate unconsumed, raising glyoxylate which is then excreted in urine — reduced AGT activity raises urinary glyoxylate

causal:influence:airway_resistance:posit.evidence: "The higher the airway resistance or the inspiratory flow rate, the more negative (rightward) would be the intrapleural pressure excursion ... and the larger the area" (West's Respiratory Physiology, 11th ed., ch 7)
causal:influence:airway_resistance:posit.mechanism: higher airway resistance enlarges the viscous (resistive) work area of the breathing-cycle pressure-volume loop, increasing work of breathing

causal:influence:aldosterone:negative:pl.evidence: StatPearls NBK470339 (Physiology, Aldosterone): aldosterone increases distal/collecting-duct potassium secretion/excretion, lowering plasma potassium. Boron & Boulpaep; Guyton & Hall; HumMod aldosterone module
causal:influence:aldosterone:negative:pl.mechanism: aldosterone stimulates renal distal/collecting-duct K+ secretion (kaliuresis), lowering plasma K+; spironolactone->hyperkalemia and Addison/Conn corroborate the direction

causal:influence:alpha_aminoadipic_semia.evidence: Hyperlysinemia OMIM 238700; AASS deficiency GeneReviews; MedlinePlus hyperlysinemia: hyperlysinemia due to AASS deficiency; overflow aminoaciduria mechanism (Boron & Boulpaep, renal amino acid handling); Wiley JIMD Reports 2023 PMID hyperlysinemia case — lysinuria in AASS deficiency. | intervention: do(AASS loss-of-function) — hyperlysinemia OMIM 238700
causal:influence:alpha_aminoadipic_semia.mechanism: AASS (lysine-ketoglutarate reductase/saccharopine dehydrogenase) initiates lysine catabolism; AASS LoF -> hyperlysinemia -> overflow lysinuria (plasma lysine exceeds renal tubular reabsorption capacity). do(AASS LoF) -> urinary lysine excretion rises.

causal:influence:alpha_n_acetylgalactosa.evidence: PMID 14685826; (Abstract (Structural and immunocytochemical studies on alpha-N-acetylgalactosaminidase deficiency (Schindler/Kanzaki disease))); “Immunocytochemical analysis revealed that the main lysosomal accumulated material in cultured fibroblasts from patients with Kanzaki disease is Tn-antigen.” | do(loss of NAGA) accumulates Tn-antigen, so NAGA activity negatively affects Tn-antigen level. [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:alpha_n_acetylgalactosa.mechanism: alpha-N-acetylgalactosaminidase (NAGA) cleaves terminal alpha-GalNAc from Tn-antigen glycopeptides; LoF deficiency (Kanzaki disease) leads to lysosomal Tn-antigen accumulation -> NAGA activity lowers Tn-antigen

causal:influence:alveolar_ventilation:ne.evidence: "If the alveolar ventilation is halved (and CO2 production remains unchanged) ... the alveolar and arterial PCO2 will double" (West's Respiratory Physiology, 11th ed., ch 2)  ||  The resulting hyperventilation reduces the PCO2 in the blood and therefore in the CSF
causal:influence:alveolar_ventilation:ne.mechanism: alveolar and arterial PCO2 are virtually identical, so the inverse alveolar-ventilation relation carries through; halving alveolar ventilation doubles arterial PCO2

causal:influence:aromatase_activity:nega.evidence: Williams Textbook of Endocrinology (aromatase deficiency: accumulation of androgenic precursors incl. androstenedione, low estrogens); substrate-consumption sign convention
causal:influence:aromatase_activity:nega.mechanism: aromatase consumes androstenedione as substrate; higher aromatase activity lowers the androstenedione pool (substrate consumption), while aromatase deficiency raises androgens

causal:influence:arterial_pco2:negative:.evidence: When the blood PCO2 rises, CO2 diffuses into the CSF from the cerebral blood vessels, liberating H+ ions that stimulate the chemoreceptors
causal:influence:arterial_pco2:negative:.mechanism: rising blood PCO2 -> CO2 diffuses across blood-brain barrier into CSF -> liberates H+ -> CSF pH falls

causal:influence:arterial_ph:positive:ce.evidence: Boron & Boulpaep; Guyton & Hall: acid-base status shifts K+ across the cell membrane (acidosis raises, alkalosis lowers plasma K+)
causal:influence:arterial_ph:positive:ce.mechanism: alkalosis (high pH) drives H+ out of and K+ into cells via H+/K+ exchange and stimulated Na/K-ATPase; acidosis (low pH) reverses this

causal:influence:arterial_ph:positive:re.evidence: "Acute increases in hydrogen ion concentration of the extracellular fluid (acidosis) reduce potassium secretion, whereas decreased hydrogen ion concentration (alkalosis) increases potassium secretion" -- Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology, ch 29 (Renal Regulation), p 372
causal:influence:arterial_ph:positive:re.mechanism: increased H+ (low pH/acidosis) reduces principal-cell Na/K-ATPase activity and K+ secretion; alkalosis (high pH) increases distal K+ secretion

causal:influence:aspartoacylase_activity.evidence: Canavan disease (ASPA deficiency, OMIM 271900) — elevated CSF N-acetylaspartate and decreased CNS aspartate; Blau et al., Physician's Guide to Inherited Metabolic Diseases (Canavan disease: ASPA deficiency impairs myelin N-acetylaspartate hydrolysis; aspartate as product falls); Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry (N-acetylaspartate hydrolysis by aspartoacylase yields aspartate). | intervention: do(ASPA LoF) — Canavan disease: CSF aspartate falls
causal:influence:aspartoacylase_activity.mechanism: Aspartoacylase (ASPA) hydrolyzes N-acetylaspartate (NAA) to aspartate + acetate in oligodendrocytes; ASPA deficiency (Canavan disease) blocks this hydrolysis, reducing aspartate production from NAA while NAA accumulates; aspartate is the direct product of ASPA and falls when the enzyme is absent.

causal:influence:bckdh_activity:negative.evidence: Maple syrup urine disease (MSUD; BCKDHA/BCKDHB/DBT, OMIM 248600); Scriver's OMMBID, MSUD chapter: urine organic acid analysis reveals elevated 2-oxoacids and their hydroxylated derivatives; StatPearls NBK557773 | intervention: genetic LoF of BCKDHA, BCKDHB, or DBT gene (biallelic mutation; autosomal recessive MSUD)
causal:influence:bckdh_activity:negative.mechanism: The BCKDH complex decarboxylates 3-methyl-2-oxovalerate (the alpha-keto acid of isoleucine); BCKDH deficiency (MSUD) causes 3-methyl-2-oxovalerate to accumulate and be side-reduced by LDH to 2-hydroxy-3-methylvaleric acid (alpha-hydroxy-beta-methylvalerate), excreted in urine — reduced BCKDH activity raises urinary 2-hydroxy-3-methylvalerate

causal:influence:beta1_adrenergic_chrono.evidence: Curated by G. Gkoutos (2026), heart_rate_physio_with_T3_example — "β responsiveness ↑ → sympathetic effects amplified → HR tendency ↑". Evidence code ECO:0000305 (curator inference used in manual assertion).
causal:influence:beta1_adrenergic_chrono.mechanism: beta1-adrenergic chronotropic responsiveness (quality) -> for a given sympathetic/catecholamine input, stronger cAMP-PKA-mediated If and L-type Ca current modulation in the SA node -> larger increase in phase-4 slope and firing rate -> heart rate. (First-order shadow of the modulation_edge below.)

causal:influence:beta_ketothiolase_activ.evidence: Beta-ketothiolase deficiency (ACAT1, OMIM 203750); Fukao et al., Orphanet (beta-KT deficiency): tiglylglycine elevated in plasma and urine acylglycine analysis during metabolic decompensation; Saudubray, Inborn Metabolic Diseases | intervention: genetic LoF of ACAT1 gene (biallelic mutation; autosomal recessive beta-ketothiolase deficiency)
causal:influence:beta_ketothiolase_activ.mechanism: ACAT1 deficiency backs up isoleucine catabolism upstream, causing tiglyl-CoA (2-methylcrotonoyl-CoA) to accumulate and be conjugated with glycine to tiglylglycine — reduced ACAT1 activity raises plasma tiglylglycine

causal:influence:blood_volume:positive:v.evidence: circulation.cellml venous_blood_volume/venous_average_pressure -> rate_of_blood_flow_from_veins_to_right_atrium (QVO) | textbook corroboration: OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology 2e §anp-110 (19.6: Development of the Heart) — chapter review 19.4: 'Venous return is determined by activity of the skeletal muscles, blood volume, and changes in peripheral circulation.' (lines 413–414).; OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology 2e §anp-112 (20.3: Blood Flow, Blood Pressure, and Resistance): 'As blood volume decreases, pressure and flow decrease. As blood volume increases, pressure and flow increase.'; OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology 2e §anp-156 (26.3: Water Balance): 'Decreased blood volume resulting from water loss... baroreceptors detect a decrease in blood pressure that results from decreased blood volume.'
causal:influence:blood_volume:positive:v.mechanism: raised blood volume raises mean systemic filling pressure -> venous return

causal:influence:body_weight:positive:ad.evidence: BioModels BIOMD0000000901 ChowHall2008 (fat/lean body-composition partitioning); Chow & Hall, PLoS Comput Biol 2008, PMID 18369435 [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:body_weight:positive:ad.mechanism: a fraction of gained/lost body mass is partitioned into the fat compartment, so fat mass tracks body weight (body-composition partition)

causal:influence:carbamoylphosphate_synt.evidence: CPS1 deficiency ScienceDirect overview — CPS1 LoF causes hyperammonemia with low citrulline; PMC11513499 retrospective CPS1 cohort — low plasma citrulline consistently; Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry, urea cycle (CPS1 step 1, OTC step 2 → citrulline); OMIM 237300 CPS1 deficiency. | intervention: CPS1 LoF (CPS1 deficiency, OMIM 237300): carbamoylphosphate synthetase 1 activity DOWN → no carbamoyl phosphate → OTC substrate absent → plasma citrulline DOWN
causal:influence:carbamoylphosphate_synt.mechanism: CPS1 catalyzes the first committed step of the urea cycle: ammonia + HCO3- + 2ATP → carbamoyl phosphate. Carbamoyl phosphate is the substrate for OTC, which produces citrulline. CPS1 LoF blocks carbamoyl phosphate production, depriving OTC of substrate, so citrulline synthesis falls.

causal:influence:carboxyhemoglobin:negat.evidence: small amounts of CO can tie up a large proportion of the Hb in the blood, thus making it unavailable for O2 carriage. If this happens, the Hb concentration and P O2 of blood may be normal, but its O2 concentration is grossly reduced
causal:influence:carboxyhemoglobin:negat.mechanism: COHb occupies Hb binding sites, making Hb unavailable for O2 carriage so O2 content falls despite normal Hb and PO2

causal:influence:cellular_adp_level:posi.evidence: Guyton & Hall, Medical Physiology, 11th ed. Ch.67 (Metabolism of Carbohydrates, and Formation of Adenosine Triphosphate) §Effect of ATP and ADP Cell Concentrations in Controlling the Rate of Glycolysis: “ADP (and AMP as well) causes the opposite change in this enzyme, greatly increasing its activity.”
causal:influence:cellular_adp_level:posi.mechanism: rising cellular ADP (energy-deficit signal) allosterically activates phosphofructokinase, raising its catalytic rate and accelerating glycolysis

causal:influence:cervical_distension:pos.evidence: Guyton & Hall, Medical Physiology, 11th ed. Ch.75 (Pituitary Hormones and Their Control by the Hypothalamus) §Oxytocin Causes Contraction of the Pregnant Uterus: “Stimulation of the cervix in a pregnant animal elicits nervous signals that pass to the hypothalamus and cause increased secretion of oxytocin”
causal:influence:cervical_distension:pos.mechanism: cervical stretch afferents signal the hypothalamus to increase oxytocin secretion (Ferguson reflex)

causal:influence:cnt1_activity:negative:.evidence: Wevers et al., J Inherit Metab Dis 2019 (SLC28A1/CNT1 biallelic LoF causes a novel inborn error of metabolism with high urinary uridine and cytidine excretion, PMID 30847922); OMIM *606207. | intervention: do(SLC28A1 LoF) — renal uridine reabsorption fails; urinary uridine rises [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:cnt1_activity:negative:.mechanism: CNT1 (SLC28A1) is the concentrative Na+/nucleoside cotransporter expressed at the apical membrane of renal proximal tubule cells; it reabsorbs uridine from the glomerular filtrate. CNT1 LoF abolishes renal uridine reabsorption, causing elevated urinary uridine excretion (uridine-cytidinuria disorder).

causal:influence:cortisol:negative:plasm.evidence: "they are reduced by glucocorticoids and in patients with cirrhosis, nephrosis, and hyperthyroidism" — Williams Textbook of Endocrinology, 14th ed., ch 15, p. 493

causal:influence:cortisol:positive:plasm.evidence: Mechanism: cortisol -> hepatic glucocorticoid receptor -> increased/permissive PLG transcription within the IL-6 acute-phase program -> higher plasma plasminogen. Citation: Jenkins GR, Seiffert D, Parmer RJ, Miles LA. Blood 1997;89(7):2394-2403 (PMID 9116283; hydrocortisone separately increased plasminogen mRNA in primary hepatocytes). Standard glucocorticoid-permissiveness for hepatic acute-phase proteins: Boron & Boulpaep, Medical Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Medical Physiology (cortisol and the acute-phase response). Hydrocortisone addition (pharmacological do()) to primary hepatocytes increases plasminogen mRNA.
causal:influence:cortisol:positive:plasm.mechanism: Glucocorticoid (cortisol/hydrocortisone) independently increases hepatic plasminogen mRNA and is permissive/potentiating for the hepatic acute-phase response (synergy with IL-6 on C/EBPbeta-class acute-phase genes), raising plasma plasminogen.

causal:influence:cpt2_activity:negative:.evidence: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 'Inherited disorders of fatty acid metabolism' (CPT-II deficiency, OMIM 255110; elevated C16/C18 acylcarnitines); Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry, carnitine shuttle
causal:influence:cpt2_activity:negative:.mechanism: CPT2 regenerates long-chain acyl-CoA from acylcarnitine at the inner mitochondrial membrane; reduced CPT2 activity backs up long-chain acylcarnitines (C16/C18) into plasma (CPT-II deficiency RAISES long-chain acylcarnitines)

causal:influence:cpt2_activity:negative:.evidence: CPT-II deficiency (OMIM 255110): GeneReviews NBK1253; Schuler et al. 'Biochemical Markers for the Diagnosis of Mitochondrial Fatty Acid Oxidation Diseases' MDPI J Clin Med 2021 (C18 acylcarnitine elevated in CPT2/CACT deficiency) | intervention: loss-of-function of CPT2 gene (CPT-II deficiency, OMIM 255110)
causal:influence:cpt2_activity:negative:.mechanism: CPT2 cleaves C18 stearoylcarnitine to regenerate stearoyl-CoA inside mitochondria; reduced CPT2 activity strands stearoylcarnitine (C18) in the cytosol and plasma (CPT-II deficiency elevates C18 stearoylcarnitine)

causal:influence:csf_ph:negative:alveola.evidence: local application of H+ or dissolved CO2 to this area stimulates breathing within a few seconds... An increase in H+ concentration stimulates ventilation, whereas a decrease inhibits it
causal:influence:csf_ph:negative:alveola.mechanism: central chemoreceptors sense brain ECF/CSF H+ -> drive respiratory center; lower pH (higher H+) stimulates breathing

causal:influence:cystinosin_activity:neg.evidence: Cystinosis (CTNS deficiency, OMIM 219800) — elevated free cystine in CSF and in cells of the CNS (cornea, brain, kidney, liver); Blau et al., Physician's Guide to Inherited Metabolic Diseases (cystinosis: CTNS lysosomal cystine transporter deficiency, cystine accumulation in all tissues including CNS); Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine (cystinosis: lysosomal storage of cystine). | intervention: do(CTNS LoF) — cystinosis
causal:influence:cystinosin_activity:neg.mechanism: Cystinosin (CTNS) is the lysosomal cystine transporter that exports cystine (the disulfide dimer of cysteine) from lysosomes into the cytoplasm; CTNS deficiency (cystinosis) causes lysosomal cystine accumulation in virtually all cell types including CNS cells, raising free cystine in CSF.

causal:influence:dhcr7_activity:positive.evidence: Wassif CA et al. Nat Genet. 1998;18:107-110; Waterham HR et al. Ann Hum Genet. 2003;67:516-534 (DHCR7 mutations in SLOS); OMIM 270400 (Smith-Lemli-Opitz syndrome); Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry, cholesterol biosynthesis (Kandutsch-Russell pathway: 7-DHC -> cholesterol via DHCR7). Intervention: DHCR7 loss-of-function (Smith-Lemli-Opitz syndrome, OMIM 270400): do(DHCR7 activity down) -> hepatic cholesterol synthesis severely reduced.
causal:influence:dhcr7_activity:positive.mechanism: DHCR7 (7-dehydrocholesterol reductase) catalyses the final step of cholesterol biosynthesis (Kandutsch-Russell pathway): reduction of 7-dehydrocholesterol to cholesterol. DHCR7 loss-of-function (Smith-Lemli-Opitz syndrome, SLOS, OMIM 270400) blocks the last enzymatic step, drastically reducing de novo cholesterol synthesis in the liver and all tissues while 7-DHC and 8-DHC accumulate.

causal:influence:dietary_linolenic_acid_.evidence: PMID 7910999; (Abstract, Results); “EPA concentrations increased by 2.5-fold in the plasma lipid fractions and neutrophil phospholipids.” | do(increase dietary alpha-linolenic acid) increases plasma EPA (+); flaxseed/ALA-rich diet raised plasma EPA 2.5-fold [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:dietary_linolenic_acid_.mechanism: dietary ALA (18:3 n-3) is elongated/desaturated to EPA (20:5 n-3); raising ALA intake raises plasma/tissue EPA

causal:influence:eg_mesangial_contractio.evidence: Wagner et al. Circ Res 2007;100:556-563 (Cx40 couples mesangial & renin cells; required for pressure control of renin); calcium paradox of renin secretion, Boron & Boulpaep Medical Physiology.
causal:influence:eg_mesangial_contractio.mechanism: Cx40 (GJA5) gap-junction coupling of extraglomerular mesangial cells to JG granular cells transmits the contractile/Ca2+ signal; rising Ca2+ in renin cells is inhibitory ("calcium paradox" of renin secretion), reducing renin exocytosis (GO:0002001 renin secretion into blood)

causal:influence:endothelial_pgi2_produc.evidence: Substances that can relax smooth muscle in the pulmonary circulation include acetylcholine, calcium channel blockers, nitric oxide, phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitors, and prostacyclin (PGI2)
causal:influence:endothelial_pgi2_produc.mechanism: prostacyclin (PGI2) relaxes pulmonary vascular smooth muscle

causal:influence:epinephrine:positive:pl.evidence: Guyton & Hall, Medical Physiology, 11th ed. Ch.78 (Insulin, Glucagon, and Diabetes Mellitus) §Role of Insulin (and Other Hormones) in Switching: “Epinephrine is especially important in increasing plasma glucose concentration during periods of stress when the sympathetic nervous system is excited”
causal:influence:epinephrine:positive:pl.mechanism: adrenal epinephrine drives hepatic glycogenolysis, releasing glucose into blood

causal:influence:epinephrine:unknown:tot.evidence: OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology 2e §anp-081 (15.3: Autonomic Reflexes and Homeostasis): 'The hormones released from the adrenal medulla—epinephrine and norepinephrine—will also bind to these receptors [adrenergic receptors on blood vessels], causing constriction and increasing blood pressure.' | textbook corroboration: OpenStax Biology 2e §bio-41.5 (41.5: Hormonal Control of Osmoregulatory Functions): 'These hormones [epinephrine and norepinephrine] function by acting directly on the smooth muscles of blood vessels to constrict them.'
causal:influence:epinephrine:unknown:tot.mechanism: circulating epinephrine from the adrenal medulla binds adrenergic receptors on systemic blood vessel walls, causing smooth muscle constriction and raising vascular resistance

causal:influence:erythroblast_proliferat.evidence: OmniPath ligrec ICAM4->ITGAV is_stimulation=True, PMID 11435317 (15355350); Chasis & Mohandas (2008) Blood 112:470-478, PMID 18650462. Manwani & Bieker (2008) PMID 18282516. [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:erythroblast_proliferat.mechanism: juxtacrine feedback: expanding erythroblasts present ICAM4 to macrophage alphaV integrin, assembling/stabilizing the island and sustaining macrophage support (quality: erythroblast number/proliferation -> disposition: ICAM4-alphaV adhesion -> process: GO:0007157 heterophilic cell-cell adhesion / island assembly -> quality: macrophage support activity)

causal:influence:erythrocyte_pyruvate_ki.evidence: PKLR deficiency OMIM 266200; Williams Hematology 'Pyruvate Kinase Deficiency' (elevated serum LDH in haemolytic episodes); Harrison's 'Haemolytic Anaemia' (LDH released from lysing RBCs is a marker of haemolysis). | intervention: do(erythrocyte_pyruvate_kinase_activity ↓) — PKLR deficiency OMIM 266200
causal:influence:erythrocyte_pyruvate_ki.mechanism: Red blood cells contain high concentrations of LDH; haemolysis caused by PKLR deficiency releases intracellular LDH into plasma, elevating serum LDH. This haemolytic source of plasma LDH is independent of the muscle-damage leakage pathway.

causal:influence:erythropoietin:positive.evidence: Kautz et al. 2014 Nat Genet 46:678-684 (EPO/STAT5-dependent ERFE; PMID 24880340) [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:erythropoietin:positive.mechanism: EPO drives erythroblast proliferation and, via STAT5, induces erythroferrone secretion — raising the erythropoietic iron-demand signal

causal:influence:ferroportin_activity:po.evidence: Parmar2019 BioModels MODEL1805140003 (ferroportin flux -> plasma Fe; PMID 30608934); Boron & Boulpaep Medical Physiology [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:ferroportin_activity:po.mechanism: ferroportin is the sole cellular iron exporter; higher export from duodenal enterocytes and reticuloendothelial macrophages raises transferrin-bound plasma iron

causal:influence:free_t3:negative:plasma.evidence: "a decrease in serum cholesterol level" Williams Textbook of Endocrinology, 14th ed., ch 12, p. 366
causal:influence:free_t3:negative:plasma.mechanism: Thyroid hormones increase hepatic LDL-receptor expression and bile acid synthesis from cholesterol, reducing plasma total cholesterol

causal:influence:free_t3:positive:gi_tra.evidence: "The increased gastric emptying and intestinal motility in thyrotoxicosis appear to be responsible for slight malabsorption of fat, and these functions return to normal when a normal metabolic state has been restored." Williams Textbook of Endocrinology, 14th ed., ch 12, p. 367
causal:influence:free_t3:positive:gi_tra.mechanism: Thyroid hormones increase gastric emptying rate and intestinal motility, with normalization upon restoration of euthyroid state confirming causal direction

causal:influence:free_t3:positive:plasma.evidence: Sorensen, Hansen, Steffensen, Jensenius, Thiel. Hormonal regulation of mannan-binding lectin synthesis in hepatocytes. Clin Exp Immunol 2006;145(1):173-182, PMID 16792688 (DOI 10.1111/j.1365-2249.2006.03101.x) - VERIFIED; T3 4-fold at 1 nM, >8-fold at 100 nM, dose-dependent, P<0.001.
causal:influence:free_t3:positive:plasma.mechanism: Thyroid hormone is a strong positive transcriptional regulator of hepatic mannan-binding lectin (MBL2). In human hepatocyte (HuH-7) culture, T3 gave a ~4-fold increase in MBL at 1 nM and >8-fold at 100 nM (dose-dependent, P<0.001); T4 similar, less potent. core->analyte downstream sink (free T3 -> circulating MBL via hepatocyte production), no new feedback-core path. Within-scale ORGAN_SYSTEM->ORGAN_SYSTEM.

All of these abnormalities are relieved by treatment." Williams Textbook of Endocrinology, 14th ed., ch 13
causal:influence:free_t4:positive:core_t.mechanism: thyroid hormone drives thermogenesis; loss of T4 lowers core temperature and causes cold intolerance; T4 replacement corrects

causal:influence:free_t4:positive:metabo.evidence: "The decrease in energy metabolism and heat production is reflected in a low basal metabolic rate, decreased appetite, cold intolerance, and slightly low basal body temperature." Williams Textbook of Endocrinology, 14th ed., ch 13
causal:influence:free_t4:positive:metabo.mechanism: thyroid hormones drive mitochondrial thermogenesis and oxidative metabolism; loss of T4 lowers BMR; T4 replacement reverses

causal:influence:galt_activity:negative:.evidence: Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry Ch. 15 (Leloir pathway: GALT is the galactose-1-P uridylyltransferase step); Scriver's OMMBID (classic galactosemia, OMIM 230400 — hypergalactosaemia, galactosuria); Boron & Boulpaep Medical Physiology (galactose metabolism in liver). | intervention: GALT loss-of-function (classic galactosemia, OMIM 230400): do(galt_activity↓) → plasma galactose accumulates (hypergalactosaemia)
causal:influence:galt_activity:negative:.mechanism: GALT (galactose-1-phosphate uridylyltransferase) catalyzes the exchange reaction: galactose-1-phosphate + UDP-glucose → glucose-1-phosphate + UDP-galactose (second step of the Leloir galactose pathway). GALT LoF (classic galactosemia, OMIM 230400) → galactose-1-P accumulates, galactose cannot be cleared → plasma galactose rises markedly on a galactose-containing diet. GALT activity ↑ → galactose-1-P converted to UDP-Gal → pathway flux increases → plasma galactose ↓.

causal:influence:gch1_activity:positive:.evidence: Blau et al., Physician's Guide to Inherited Metabolic Diseases (GCH1 deficiency / Dopa-responsive dystonia: LOW CSF neopterin AND tetrahydrobiopterin — GCH1 is the rate-limiting upstream enzyme for all pterins including neopterin); GCH1 deficiency OMIM 600225; Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry (GTP cyclohydrolase I: GTP -> 7,8-dihydroneopterin triphosphate). | intervention: do(GCH1 LoF) — GCH1 deficiency (Dopa-responsive dystonia): neopterin falls
causal:influence:gch1_activity:positive:.mechanism: GTP cyclohydrolase I (GCH1) catalyzes the first committed step in BH4 biosynthesis, converting GTP to 7,8-dihydroneopterin triphosphate (D-NH2P); D-NH2P is the shared precursor of both BH4 and neopterin; reduced GCH1 activity (Dopa-responsive dystonia, GCH1 deficiency) lowers D-NH2P, reducing both CSF neopterin and BH4.

causal:influence:gfr:negative:urinary_ng.evidence: Mori & Nakao, AJKD 2007 (NGAL as a marker of kidney damage). Paragas et al., Kidney Int 2011 PMID 32110797 (impaired tubular reabsorption is the main mechanism of elevated urinary NGAL after AKI). Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine (NGAL as early AKI biomarker). | intervention: do(GFR DOWN via AKI) — cisplatin nephrotoxicity, ischemia-reperfusion injury, or contrast nephropathy consistently raise urinary NGAL [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:gfr:negative:urinary_ng.mechanism: GFR decline in acute kidney injury (AKI) reflects tubular cell injury; injured tubular cells in the thick ascending limb, distal tubule and collecting duct markedly upregulate LCN2 (NGAL) expression and secrete it into the urine. NGAL rises within 2 hours of ischemic or nephrotoxic AKI, before creatinine changes. Lower GFR from acute tubular injury reliably predicts higher urinary NGAL.

causal:influence:gfr:negative:urinary_or.evidence: Wang et al., Nephrology 2020 (urinary orosomucoid 1 as biomarker of renal impairment in T2D, threshold 2.53 mg/L). Torffvit et al., Scand J Clin Lab Invest 2005 (monitoring urinary orosomucoid in acute inflammation with albuminuria). Brenner & Rector's The Kidney (tubular biomarkers in kidney disease). | intervention: do(GFR DOWN) — diabetic nephropathy or glomerulonephritis lowers GFR and raises urinary orosomucoid [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:gfr:negative:urinary_or.mechanism: Orosomucoid (alpha-1-acid glycoprotein, MW ~41 kDa) is normally retained by the glomerular filtration barrier; glomerular injury accompanying GFR decline increases glomerular permeability, allowing orosomucoid to pass into the filtrate and appear in urine. Lower GFR indicates more glomerular dysfunction and more urinary orosomucoid. The relationship is well-documented in diabetic nephropathy and proteinuric CKD.

causal:influence:ggt1_activity:negative:.evidence: Gamma-glutamyl transpeptidase deficiency OMIM (GGT1 deficiency, glutathionuria/elevated gamma-glutamyl compounds); PMC5974402 (gamma-glutamyl transpeptidase deficiency caused by large homozygous deletion in GGT1): patients have elevated urinary glutathione and gamma-glutamyl compounds; PMC1852094 (gamma-glutamyl cycle, GGT1 role in degrading gamma-glutamyl peptides); Lehninger (gamma-glutamyl cycle). | intervention: do(GGT1 loss-of-function) — gamma-glutamyl transpeptidase deficiency
causal:influence:ggt1_activity:negative:.mechanism: GGT1 (gamma-glutamyltransferase 1/glutathione hydrolase 1) cleaves the gamma-glutamyl group from glutathione and gamma-glutamyl amino acids. GGT1 deficiency (gamma-glutamyl transpeptidase deficiency) blocks processing of gamma-glutamyl compounds in the gamma-glutamyl cycle; gamma-glutamyl amino acids including gamma-glutamylphenylalanine accumulate and spill into urine. do(GGT1 LoF) -> urinary gamma-glutamylphenylalanine rises.

causal:influence:gi_sympathetic_tone:neg.evidence: Sympathetic stimulation, by contrast, has a direct effect on essentially all the gastrointestinal tract to cause intense vasoconstriction of the arterioles with greatly decreased blood flow.
causal:influence:gi_sympathetic_tone:neg.mechanism: sympathetic norepinephrine causes arteriolar vasoconstriction in splanchnic bed → decreased blood flow

causal:influence:glomerular_colloid_osmo.evidence: Guyton & Hall, Medical Physiology, 11th ed. Ch.26 (Urine Formation by the Kidneys: I. Glomerular Filtration, Renal Blood Flow, and Their Control) §Increased Glomerular Capillary Colloid Osmotic Pressure Decreases GFR: “Increasing the arterial plasma colloid osmotic pressure raises the glomerular capillary colloid osmotic pressure, which in turn decreases GFR.”
causal:influence:glomerular_colloid_osmo.mechanism: rising glomerular plasma colloid osmotic pressure opposes filtration, lowering net filtration pressure and GFR

causal:influence:glut4_expression:positi.evidence: CB-MET-008. Intervention: two tissue-specific Slc2a4/GLUT4 knockouts in mouse — muscle-specific KO (Zisman A et al., Nat Med 2000;6:924-928, PMID:10932232) and adipose-specific KO (Abel ED et al., Nature 2001;409:729-733, PMID:11217863). Measured endpoint: insulin-stimulated glucose uptake — muscle GLUT4 KO nearly abolishes insulin-stimulated muscle glucose uptake with glucose intolerance/insulin resistance; adipose GLUT4 KO impairs adipocyte uptake and induces secondary muscle/liver insulin resistance. Context: mouse skeletal muscle/adipose, chronic total-GLUT4-protein manipulation. do(GLUT4 expression down) => peripheral glucose uptake down, sign +.
causal:influence:glut4_expression:positi.mechanism: GLUT4 (SLC2A4) is the insulin-responsive glucose transporter; total GLUT4 protein sets the translocatable pool available for insulin-stimulated peripheral glucose disposal (quality: GLUT4 expression level -> disposition: insulin-responsive facilitated glucose transport capacity -> process: insulin-stimulated GLUT4 translocation and glucose transport -> quality: peripheral glucose uptake rate). Distinct do() from the mechanistic-model glut4_membrane_translocation -> peripheral_glucose_uptake edge (chronic total expression vs acute translocated fraction).

causal:influence:glutamine_synthetase_ac.evidence: Congenital glutamine synthetase deficiency, OMIM:610015 — LoF causes markedly reduced CSF glutamine, which is the primary clinical feature causing neonatal encephalopathy
causal:influence:glutamine_synthetase_ac.mechanism: RHEA:16169 (EC 6.3.1.2): L-glutamate + NH4(+) + ATP = L-glutamine + ADP + phosphate + H(+); CSF glutamine is low because brain GLUL is the primary enzyme maintaining CSF glutamine levels

causal:influence:heparan_alpha_glucosami.evidence: Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry Ch. 7 (heparan sulfate catabolism; HGSNAT acetyltransferase step); Sanfilippo C / MPS IIIC OMIM 252930; Neufeld & Muenzer in Scriver's Metabolic Bases: HGSNAT is a membrane-bound lysosomal acetyltransferase; deficiency causes HS storage in CNS; urinary HS elevated | intervention: do(HGSNAT activity ↓) = Sanfilippo C / MPS IIIC (OMIM 252930): heparan sulfate accumulates in lysosomes; urinary HS elevated; progressive neurodegeneration
causal:influence:heparan_alpha_glucosami.mechanism: HGSNAT (heparan-alpha-glucosaminide N-acetyltransferase) acetylates the free amino group of terminal alpha-glucosamine in heparan sulfate (a prerequisite for its removal by alpha-N-acetylglucosaminidase). HGSNAT deficiency blocks heparan sulfate degradation — Sanfilippo syndrome type C (MPS IIIC). Heparan sulfate accumulates.

causal:influence:hepatic_ldl_receptor_ac.evidence: Brown & Goldstein Science 1986 (receptor-mediated LDL uptake delivers cholesterol intracellularly; LDLR is the regulated step); BioModels BIOMD0000000434 (McAuley2012) | textbook corroboration: Wong, Cells: Molecules and Mechanisms §wong-11.7 (Receptor-mediated Endocytosis - Undeclared): LDL receptor-mediated endocytosis delivers LDL to lysosome → acid hydrolases liberate free cholesterol and amino acids from lipoprotein → cholesterol delivered to hepatocyte
causal:influence:hepatic_ldl_receptor_ac.mechanism: hepatic LDL uptake is RECEPTOR-GATED: LDLR-mediated endocytosis -> lysosomal hydrolysis -> free cholesterol delivered to the hepatocyte regulatory pool. The rate-limiting, regulated determinant of uptake is LDLR surface activity (not plasma LDL directly): with LDLR lost (FH) the hepatocyte is cholesterol-DEPLETED despite high plasma LDL.

causal:influence:hmgcl_activity:negative.evidence: PMC7358667 (HMG-CoA lyase deficiency, HMGCL LoF, OMIM 246450; elevated C5-OH and C6-DC acylcarnitines on NBS; 3-methylglutarylcarnitine detected); HRSA newborn screening '3-Hydroxy-3-Methylglutaryl-CoA Lyase Deficiency' | intervention: HMGCL LoF (HMG-CoA lyase deficiency, OMIM 246450)
causal:influence:hmgcl_activity:negative.mechanism: HMGCL (3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-CoA lyase) cleaves HMG-CoA to acetoacetate + acetyl-CoA in leucine catabolism and ketogenesis; LoF causes 3-methylglutaryl-CoA accumulation, conjugation to carnitine as 3-methylglutarylcarnitine (C6-DC), elevating plasma methylglutarylcarnitine — NBS marker of HMGCL deficiency

causal:influence:hoga1_activity:positive.evidence: Primary Hyperoxaluria Type 3 — GeneReviews NBK316514; HOGA1 gene MedlinePlus Genetics; Cellular degradation of HOGA1 leads to absolute deficiency in PH3; 4-Hydroxy-2-oxoglutarate Aldolase Inactivity in PH3 PMC3418427; PH3 cohort study PMC11753311 (childhood nephrolithiasis, risk of renal impairment). Disease: primary hyperoxaluria type 3 (OMIM 613616). | intervention: genetic LoF of HOGA1: urinary oxalate rises -> calcium oxalate nephro­calcinosis -> GFR decreases; HOGA1 activity +(+)-> GFR [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:hoga1_activity:positive.mechanism: HOGA1 (4-hydroxy-2-oxoglutarate aldolase) is a mitochondrial enzyme in the hydroxyproline degradation pathway; HOGA1 LoF causes primary hyperoxaluria type 3 (PH3), characterised by excess urinary oxalate excretion. Calcium oxalate crystals deposit in renal tubules (nephrocalcinosis) and form urolithiasis, progressively reducing glomerular filtration rate (GFR). Higher HOGA1 activity prevents oxalate overproduction and protects GFR.

causal:influence:il1beta:positive:core_t.evidence: Boron & Boulpaep Medical Physiology (endogenous pyrogens IL-1/IL-6/TNF -> hypothalamic PGE2 -> fever); Janeway's Immunobiology | perturbation: i.p. recombinant IL-1beta evokes fever in wild-type mice (opened PMC2192408) — controlled administration of the source raises core temperature | textbook corroboration: OpenStax Biology 2e §bio-33.3 (Homeostasis): 'When a bacterium is destroyed by phagocytic leukocytes, chemicals called endogenous pyrogens are released into the blood. These pyrogens circulate to the hypothalamus and reset the thermostat. This allows the body's temperature to increase in what is commonly called a fever.'; OpenStax Biology 2e §bio-42.1 (42.1: Innate Immune Response): 'Cytokines also increase the core body temperature, causing a fever' — IL-1beta is a principal pro-inflammatory cytokine driving pyrogenic fever.
causal:influence:il1beta:positive:core_t.mechanism: IL-1beta is an endogenous pyrogen -> hypothalamic PGE2 -> raised thermoregulatory set point (fever)

causal:influence:il6:negative:hepatic_ig.evidence: "IL6 has been demonstrated to activate SOCS3; this provides a pathway for inflammation to inhibit IGF1 production because SOCS3 is a negative regulator of the JAK2/STAT5 GH signal transduction pathway" — Williams Textbook of Endocrinology, 14th ed., ch 25, p. 979. Study: De Benedetti et al., transgenic murine model expressing excessive IL6 demonstrated IL6-mediated decrease in IGF1 production.
causal:influence:il6:negative:hepatic_ig.mechanism: IL-6 activates SOCS3, which is a negative regulator of the JAK2/STAT5 GH signal transduction pathway in hepatocytes, thereby reducing IGF1 production; additionally IL-6 reduces IGFBP3 levels increasing IGF1 clearance

causal:influence:il6:positive:plasma_alp.evidence: AAT is a prototype liver-derived acute-phase protein whose plasma concentration increases 3-4 fold during inflammation; IL-6 is the primary inducer of hepatocyte acute-phase protein synthesis. StatPearls 'Physiology, Acute Phase Reactants' (NCBI Bookshelf NBK519570); Guyton & Hall, Medical Physiology, 11th ed., acute-phase response. Consistent with existing il6 -> c_reactive_protein/haptoglobin/fibrinogen (+) edges in the map.
causal:influence:il6:positive:plasma_alp.mechanism: Alpha-1-antitrypsin (SERPINA1) is the prototypical hepatic positive acute-phase reactant; plasma AAT rises 3-4 fold during inflammation. IL-6 (JAK1/STAT3 in hepatocytes, the same axis driving CRP/haptoglobin/fibrinogen already in this model) up-regulates hepatic SERPINA1 synthesis. do(IL-6 up) -> hepatic AAT synthesis up -> plasma AAT up.

causal:influence:inhibin:negative:gonado.evidence: "This hormone [inhibin] has a strong direct effect on the anterior pituitary gland to inhibit the secretion of FSH." — Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology, Ch. 80, p. 1008
causal:influence:inhibin:negative:gonado.mechanism: Sertoli-cell inhibin has a strong direct effect on the anterior pituitary to selectively inhibit FSH secretion (spermatogenesis feedback)

causal:influence:interstitial_fluid_coll.evidence: Guyton & Hall, Medical Physiology, 11th ed. Ch.25 (The Body Fluid Compartments: Extracellular and Intracellular Fluids; Interstitial Fluid and Edema) §Washdown of the Interstitial Fluid Protein as a Safety Factor: “the interstitial fluid colloid osmotic pressure caused by the proteins tends to draw fluid out of the capillaries, decreasing the interstitial fluid proteins lowers the net filtration force”
causal:influence:interstitial_fluid_coll.mechanism: interstitial protein-driven colloid osmotic pressure (pif) pulls fluid out of capillaries, adding to net filtration force

causal:influence:kndy_dynorphin:negative.evidence: "dynorphin (or possibly enkephalin in humans), which inhibits kisspeptin secretion" and "treatment with a neurokinin B agonist and dynorphin antagonist can recover suppressed GnRH and LH secretion" Williams Textbook of Endocrinology, 14th ed., ch 7, p 166, 169
causal:influence:kndy_dynorphin:negative.mechanism: dynorphin co-expressed in KNDy neurons inhibits kisspeptin secretion via kappa-opioid receptors; NK3R agonist plus dynorphin antagonist recovers suppressed GnRH/LH

causal:influence:l2hgdh_activity:negativ.evidence: L-2-hydroxyglutaric aciduria (L2HGDH, OMIM 236792); Saudubray, Inborn Metabolic Diseases — biochemical hallmark is elevated L-2-hydroxyglutaric acid in CSF, urine, and plasma; Struys et al., J. Inherit. Metab. Dis. 2005 (PMC10129278 review: CSF L-2-HG is relatively higher than plasma and urine) | intervention: genetic LoF of L2HGDH gene (biallelic mutation; autosomal recessive L-2-hydroxyglutaric aciduria)
causal:influence:l2hgdh_activity:negativ.mechanism: L-2-hydroxyglutarate dehydrogenase (L2HGDH) oxidises L-2-hydroxyglutarate to 2-oxoglutarate (alpha-ketoglutarate); loss-of-function leaves L-2-HG unconsumed, causing it to accumulate in mitochondria and body fluids including CSF — reduced L2HGDH activity raises CSF L-2-hydroxyglutarate concentration

causal:influence:lepr_signaling:negative.evidence: "Stimulation of leptin receptors in these hypothalamic nuclei initiates multiple actions that decrease fat storage, including (1) decreased production in the hypothalamus of appetite stimulators, such as NPY and AGRP" — Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology, Ch. 71, p. 868-870
causal:influence:lepr_signaling:negative.mechanism: LEPR signalling stimulates POMC/alpha-MSH (anorexigenic) and inhibits AGRP-NPY, reducing orexigenic appetite drive

causal:influence:lh:positive:estradiol.evidence: BioModels BIOMD0000000494 (Roblitz2013, LH->E2); Boron & Boulpaep two-cell two-gonadotropin model | textbook corroboration: OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology 2e §anp-161 (27.3: Anatomy and Physiology of the Female Reproductive System): 'LH also stimulates the granulosa and theca cells of the follicles to produce the sex steroid hormone estradiol'; OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology 2e §anp-162 (27.4: Development of the Male and Female Reproductive Systems): 'During puberty, the release of LH and FSH from the anterior pituitary stimulates the gonads to produce sex hormones in both male and female adolescents'; 'the dominant follicle produces more estrogen, triggering positive feedback and the LH surge'.; OpenStax Biology 2e §bio-37.3 (37.3: Regulation of Body Processes): 'LH also plays a role in the development of ova, induction of ovulation, and stimulation of estradiol and progesterone production by the ovaries.'; OpenStax Biology 2e §bio-43.3 (43.3: Human Reproductive Anatomy and Gametogenesis): 'LH also plays a role in the development of ova, induction of ovulation, and stimulation of estradiol...and progesterone production by the ovaries.'
causal:influence:lh:positive:estradiol.mechanism: LH drives thecal androgen production aromatised to estradiol; granulosa/Leydig steroidogenesis

causal:influence:lh:positive:intratestic.evidence: "In normal men, LH stimulates intratesticular testosterone concentrations that are approximately 100- to 200-fold higher than serum testosterone concentrations and correlate with circulating LH concentrations. Administration of various combinations of exogenous testosterone, progestin, and GnRH antagonist to induce gonadotropin deficiency in male contraception trials suppressed intratesticular testosterone by 98%… Short-term administration of hCG (LH-like activity) in normal men with experimental gonadotropin deficiency resulted in a dose-dependent increase in intratesticular testosterone." Williams Textbook of Endocrinology, 14th ed., ch 19, p 683
causal:influence:lh:positive:intratestic.mechanism: LH binds LHCGR on Leydig cells → Gs/cAMP/PKA → StAR + CYP11A1 + CYP17A1 → testosterone biosynthesis and secretion into testicular interstitium

causal:influence:lipoprotein_lipase_acti.evidence: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, Disorders of Lipoprotein Metabolism; OMIM 238600 (LPL deficiency); Boron & Boulpaep Medical Physiology | intervention: LPL loss-of-function (familial chylomicronemia, OMIM 238600): do(LPL activity down) -> non-HDL cholesterol up
causal:influence:lipoprotein_lipase_acti.mechanism: LPL clears TG-rich lipoprotein particles (chylomicrons, VLDL, IDL); these particles carry the bulk of non-HDL cholesterol. LPL loss-of-function causes chylomicron and VLDL accumulation, raising non-HDL cholesterol.

causal:influence:macrophage_activation:p.evidence: OmniPath ligrec IL6->IL6R / IL6R_IL6ST consensus_stimulation=True (refs SIGNOR:8676083; ICELLNET:9143707); Janeway's Immunobiology 9th ed.
causal:influence:macrophage_activation:p.mechanism: macrophage IL-6 -> IL6R/IL6ST(gp130) on CD4 T cell -> STAT3 (with TGF-beta) -> RORgt -> Th17 differentiation/activation (GO:0070102 IL-6-mediated signaling)

causal:influence:mc4r_activity:positive:.evidence: "Deleting MC4Rs in autonomic (cholinergic) neurons lowers energy expenditure and increases adiposity" and "Selective deletion or re-expression of MC4R expression in cholinergic neurons produces...failure to increase adipose tissue UCP1, an impairment of diet-induced thermogenesis" Williams Textbook of Endocrinology, 14th ed., ch 39, p 1236/1561
causal:influence:mc4r_activity:positive:.mechanism: MC4R in sympathetic preganglionic neurons (intermediolateral cell column) directly drives sympathetic outflow; MC4R deletion in cholinergic neurons impairs diet-induced thermogenesis

causal:influence:mcad_activity:negative:.evidence: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 'Inherited disorders of fatty acid metabolism' (MCAD deficiency, OMIM 201450; elevated C6-C10 acylcarnitines, esp. octanoylcarnitine C8); Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry, beta-oxidation spiral
causal:influence:mcad_activity:negative:.mechanism: MCAD dehydrogenates medium-chain acyl-CoA in the beta-oxidation spiral; reduced activity backs up medium-chain acyl-CoA, which is esterified to medium-chain acylcarnitine and exported to plasma (MCAD deficiency RAISES medium-chain acylcarnitines)

causal:influence:mcad_activity:negative:.evidence: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine (MCAD deficiency; C8 octanoylcarnitine is the diagnostic newborn-screening marker, OMIM 201450)
causal:influence:mcad_activity:negative:.mechanism: octanoylcarnitine (C8) is the principal acylcarnitine accumulating proximal to the MCAD block; reduced MCAD activity raises plasma C8

causal:influence:mcad_activity:negative:.evidence: PMC6091831 (MCAD deficiency; elevated C8 and related C8:1 species); Wikipedia 'Medium-chain acyl-coenzyme A dehydrogenase deficiency' (characteristic pattern includes C8:1 alongside C8, C6, C10) | intervention: ACADM LoF (MCAD deficiency, OMIM 201450)
causal:influence:mcad_activity:negative:.mechanism: MCAD oxidizes medium-chain acyl-CoA including cis-4-octenoyl-CoA and trans-2-octenoyl-CoA; reduced MCAD activity allows C8:1 unsaturated species to accumulate and be trapped as octenoylcarnitine (C8:1) in plasma, part of the MCAD deficiency acylcarnitine profile

causal:influence:metabolic_rate:positive.evidence: thermoregulation: metabolic rate is the source term for metabolic heat production | textbook corroboration: OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology 2e §anp-143 (24.7: Energy and Heat Balance): 10% of daily energy expenditure is for body thermoregulation/temperature control; metabolic rate links to heat generation
causal:influence:metabolic_rate:positive.mechanism: increased oxidative metabolism dissipates energy as heat (obligatory thermogenesis)

causal:influence:mevalonate_kinase_activ.evidence: Hoffmann et al., Mevalonate kinase deficiency / mevalonic aciduria (PMC1475558, PMC4184310); OMIM 610377 (MEVA) / OMIM 251170 (MVK gene): hallmark diagnostic feature is highly elevated urinary mevalonic acid; Saudubray, Inborn Metabolic Diseases | intervention: Mevalonate kinase deficiency / mevalonic aciduria (MVK loss-of-function, OMIM 610377)
causal:influence:mevalonate_kinase_activ.mechanism: Mevalonate kinase (MVK) phosphorylates mevalonate to 5-phosphomevalonate in the isoprenoid/cholesterol biosynthesis pathway; deficiency causes mevalonate to accumulate and be excreted in urine (mevalonic aciduria) — reduced MVK activity raises urinary mevalonate

causal:influence:mevalonate_kinase_activ.evidence: Hoffmann GF et al. J Inherit Metab Dis. 1993;16:872-879 (mevalonic aciduria, MVK LoF, impaired cholesterol synthesis); OMIM 251170 (mevalonic aciduria); PMC4867845 (urinary mevalonate as diagnostic marker); Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry, isoprenoid/cholesterol biosynthesis (mevalonate kinase as second committed step). Intervention: MVK loss-of-function (mevalonic aciduria, OMIM 251170): do(MVK activity down) -> hepatic cholesterol synthesis impaired.
causal:influence:mevalonate_kinase_activ.mechanism: Mevalonate kinase (MVK) phosphorylates mevalonate to mevalonate-5-phosphate, the second committed step of the mevalonate/isoprenoid pathway, which is the sole biosynthetic route to cholesterol, dolichol, ubiquinone, and prenylated proteins. MVK deficiency (mevalonic aciduria, OMIM 251170; HIDS, OMIM 260920) blocks the pathway upstream of squalene synthesis, causing mevalonate accumulation (urinary excretion) and severely impaired cholesterol synthesis in all tissues.

causal:influence:msmo1_activity:negative.evidence: Boyden LM et al. Am J Hum Genet. 2014;94:309-315 (MSMO1 deficiency; methylsterol accumulation); Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry, sterol demethylation pathway (lanosterol -> zymosterol via successive methylsterol intermediates) | intervention: MSMO1 loss-of-function (OMIM 616834): do(MSMO1 activity down) -> plasma methylsterols up
causal:influence:msmo1_activity:negative.mechanism: MSMO1 initiates C4-methylsterol demethylation (the rate-limiting oxidation of the C4-methyl group); reduced MSMO1 activity causes the entire methylsterol pool (mono- and dimethyl intermediates) to accumulate. The generic 'methylsterol' class includes all C4-methylated sterol intermediates downstream of lanosterol.

causal:influence:mttp_activity:positive:.evidence: Sharp D et al. Nature 1993 (MTTP mutations cause abetalipoproteinemia); OMIM 200100 (abetalipoproteinemia; absence of apoB-containing lipoproteins; VLDL absent); JCI 1999 PMC199271 (hepatic Mttp KO in mice: striking reduction in VLDL triglycerides; confirms MTTP as rate-limiting for hepatic VLDL secretion); Circulation Research 2016 (Contemporary aspects of MTP biology: MTP adds TG to nascent chylomicrons and VLDL; MTP inhibition reduces VLDL secretion); Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, Disorders of Lipoprotein Metabolism (abetalipoproteinemia: MTTP LoF -> complete absence of VLDL and LDL). | intervention: MTTP biallelic loss-of-function (abetalipoproteinemia, OMIM 200100): do(MTTP activity DOWN) -> VLDL assembly fails -> vldl_secretion DOWN
causal:influence:mttp_activity:positive:.mechanism: MTTP (microsomal triglyceride transfer protein) transfers triglycerides, cholesteryl esters, and phospholipids onto nascent apoB-100 in the ER lumen, enabling VLDL particle assembly and secretion by hepatocytes. Without MTTP, apoB-100 is co-translationally ubiquitinated and degraded; no VLDL (or chylomicrons) are secreted. In abetalipoproteinemia (MTTP LoF, OMIM 200100), hepatic VLDL secretion is essentially zero. More MTTP activity directly enables more VLDL assembly and secretion.

causal:influence:muscle_lipoic_acid:posi.evidence: Mayr JA et al. Am J Hum Genet 2011 (PMC3234378) — LIAS deficiency: neonatal epilepsy, lactic acidosis, reduced KGDH/PDH activities; Mayr JA et al. J Inherit Metab Dis 2014 (PMID:24777537) — lipoic acid biosynthesis defects review; Solmonson A & DeBerardinis RJ J Biol Chem 2018 (lipoate-dependent TCA enzymes); OMIM entry 607031 (LIAS). | intervention: do(LIAS LoF causing lipoic acid biosynthesis deficiency) [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:muscle_lipoic_acid:posi.mechanism: Lipoic acid (as the lipoamide prosthetic group) is covalently attached to the E2 dihydrolipoamide acyltransferase subunit of alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase (KGDH), pyruvate dehydrogenase (PDH), and branched-chain keto-acid dehydrogenase (BCKDH). Without lipoate, these complexes cannot transfer acyl groups and are inactive. LIAS (lipoic acid synthase) deficiency causes fatal neonatal-onset lactic acidosis and severely reduced KGDH and PDH activities, blocking TCA-cycle flux and pyruvate oxidation. do(LIAS LoF → muscle lipoic acid ↓) → alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase activity ↓.

causal:influence:myocardial_contractilit.evidence: Boron & Boulpaep (EF rises with contractility); Guyton & Hall (inotropic state and ejection fraction)
causal:influence:myocardial_contractilit.mechanism: EF is a load-dependent index of contractility; raising inotropy increases the fraction of EDV ejected (quality: contractility -> process: regulation of cardiac muscle contraction GO:0055117 -> quality: ejection fraction)

causal:influence:myocardial_contractilit.evidence: Boron & Boulpaep, Medical Physiology (contractility as a determinant of SV; Suga end-systolic elastance); Guyton & Hall (sympathetic inotropy shifts the function curve up)
causal:influence:myocardial_contractilit.mechanism: increased inotropic state raises systolic elastance / force at given preload and afterload, ejecting more volume (quality: contractility -> disposition: crossbridge cycling capacity -> process: regulation of cardiac muscle contraction GO:0055117 -> quality: stroke volume)

causal:influence:n_acetylglucosamine_6_s.evidence: Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry Ch. 7 (heparan sulfate catabolism); Sanfilippo D / MPS IIID OMIM 252940; Neufeld & Muenzer in Scriver's Metabolic Bases: GNS deficiency causes heparan sulfate storage — all Sanfilippo subtypes (A-D) are heparan sulfate storage diseases | intervention: do(GNS activity ↓) = Sanfilippo D / MPS IIID (OMIM 252940): heparan sulfate accumulates in lysosomes; elevated urinary HS
causal:influence:n_acetylglucosamine_6_s.mechanism: GNS (N-acetylglucosamine-6-sulfatase) cleaves 6-O-sulfate from GlcNAc-6S residues in heparan sulfate. Heparan sulfate accumulates when GNS is deficient — Sanfilippo syndrome type D (MPS IIID)

causal:influence:norepinephrine:positive.evidence: "NE, through β-adrenergic receptors, stimulates thermogenesis by brown adipose tissue" and "Basal brown adipose tissue thermogenesis and NE-stimulated and dibutyryl cAMP-stimulated thermogenesis are decreased by fetal thyroidectomy." — Williams Textbook of Endocrinology, 14th ed., ch 23, p 864
causal:influence:norepinephrine:positive.mechanism: Norepinephrine activates beta-adrenergic receptors on brown adipose tissue, stimulating UCP1/thermogenin-mediated uncoupled respiration and heat production; fetal thyroidectomy (which reduces NE responsiveness) reduces NE-stimulated and basal BAT thermogenesis

Above the plateau (~90-100 ng/mL plasma Se) the erythrocyte selenoprotein pool is saturated and d(GPx)/d(Se) approaches zero. The additive sign graph cannot express this saturation, so the + sign is asserted ONLY for the below-plateau / selenium-deficient regime, where the relationship is monotone non-decreasing (never negative).

modulation:modulation-a10be70ae3353462fb.evidence: Verified two-factor interventional measurement of the human SaO2-vs-PO2 dissociation curve with PCO2 set across 20/40/60/80 mmHg (crossed with temperature): both the CO2-Bohr coefficient and the curve position/slope change with PCO2 (P50 27.1 +/- 2.6 mmHg at 37C/40 mmHg, rising with PCO2), a measured CO2 x temperature interaction. The modulator is manipulated while the PaO2->SaO2 slope is read out. Woyke/Reinke et al., 'Effects of Carbon Dioxide and Temperature on the Oxygen-Hemoglobin Dissociation Curve of Human Blood', Front. Med. 2021, doi:10.3389/fmed.2021.808025 (DOI confirmed via web). Base edge arterial_po2->hemoglobin_o2_saturation (+) exists; additive shadow edge arterial_pco2->hemoglobin_o2_saturation (-) present and sign-consistent.
modulation:modulation-a10be70ae3353462fb.mechanism: Bohr effect (CO2 arm): CO2 (and the H+ generated from it by erythrocyte carbonic anhydrase) binds and stabilizes the deoxy/T-state of hemoglobin, lowering O2 affinity and right-shifting the oxyhemoglobin dissociation curve (P50 rises). At a fixed sub-saturating PaO2 on the steep part of the sigmoid, the right-shift reduces the local slope d(SaO2)/d(PaO2), so this is a genuine rescaling of the PaO2->SaO2 responsiveness, not an additive push. Cross-partial d2(SaO2)/d(PaO2)d(PaCO2) < 0.
